sections.content: If you're looking for real estate deals in St. Louis MO, you've landed on one of the most affordable and opportunity-rich markets in the entire country. St. Louis consistently ranks among the top Midwest cities for real estate investors, thanks to its low median home prices, diverse inventory of distressed properties, and a growing rental population. Whether you're a seasoned wholesaler or just getting started — check out this Real Estate Investing for Beginners guide if you need a solid foundation — St. Louis deserves a serious look in 2024.
St. Louis Real Estate Market Overview

St. Louis is Missouri's largest metro area, home to roughly 2.8 million people across the city and surrounding counties. The market is unique because St. Louis City is technically an independent municipality, separate from St. Louis County. This creates two distinct investing landscapes with different price points, demographics, and risk profiles. The city itself carries more distressed inventory and higher wholesale opportunity, while the county offers more stabilized neighborhoods ideal for buy-and-hold strategies.

As of 2024, the median home price in St. Louis City sits around $150,000 to $175,000, while St. Louis County averages closer to $250,000 to $280,000. These numbers are dramatically lower than national averages, which is exactly what makes this market so attractive. An investor who would need $400,000 to buy a rental in Nashville or Phoenix can enter St. Louis with a fraction of that capital and generate comparable — sometimes better — cash flow percentages.
Best Neighborhoods for Real Estate Investors in St. Louis

Not all zip codes are created equal in St. Louis. The city has some neighborhoods experiencing rapid revitalization and others that require more patience and risk tolerance. Knowing where to focus your deal-finding efforts is half the battle. You can explore neighborhood-level data and active deal opportunities on our St. Louis MO market page.
Top Neighborhoods for Wholesalers and Flippers

items: Benton Park & Benton Park West: These south city neighborhoods have seen consistent appreciation. ARVs for renovated 3-bedroom homes often land between $220,000 and $280,000, with acquisition costs as low as $60,000 to $90,000 for distressed properties.

Shaw & Tower Grove South: Hipster-adjacent zip codes with strong buyer demand. Renovated bungalows are selling fast, and investors are seeing flip margins of $40,000 to $70,000 on well-executed projects.

Baden & Riverview: North St. Louis neighborhoods with very low acquisition costs — sometimes $10,000 to $30,000 for wholesale deals — but higher risk and longer hold times. Best for experienced investors who know the micro-market.
Maplewood & Webster Groves (County): Suburban pockets with strong school ratings and consistent buyer demand. Competition is higher here, but so is deal reliability.
Dutchtown: One of the city's most active revitalization zones right now. Investors are picking up distressed duplexes and single-family homes at significant discounts before values catch up.

sections.content: Best Areas for Rental Property Investors

items: Overland & Normandy (County): Working-class suburbs with high renter density and steady demand. Section 8 landlords do particularly well here.
University City: Home to Washington University students and young professionals. Turnover is predictable, and rents are stable.
Affton & Lemay: Affordable county neighborhoods with long-term tenants and low vacancy rates.
Downtown St. Louis & Midtown: Condo and apartment rentals are gaining traction as urban demand slowly rebounds post-pandemic.

sections.content: Types of Real Estate Deals Available in St. Louis
Wholesale Deals

St. Louis is a wholesaler's playground. The city has thousands of vacant and tax-delinquent properties, many owned by absentee landlords or heirs who inherited homes they don't want. Assignment fees of $10,000 to $25,000 are common on city deals, with some north city transactions generating even higher spreads. If you're new to this strategy, start with our guide on Wholesaling Real Estate for Beginners to understand the mechanics before diving in.
Fix and Flip Opportunities

Flipping is very active in St. Louis, particularly in the south city and inner-ring suburbs. The typical flip timeline runs 3 to 5 months, and experienced investors are targeting a minimum 20% ROI on total project cost. The key is accurate ARV analysis — use our free ARV Calculator to estimate your after-repair value before you commit to any deal. Renovation costs in St. Louis run $25 to $45 per square foot for moderate rehabs, which is relatively affordable compared to coastal markets.
Buy-and-Hold Rentals

St. Louis offers some of the best cash-on-cash returns in the Midwest for buy-and-hold investors. A $120,000 property in Overland or Affton can rent for $1,100 to $1,400 per month, producing cap rates well above 8% — far exceeding what you'd find in overheated coastal cities. The city also has a strong Section 8 voucher program, giving landlords a reliable income stream backed by HUD.

Pro Tip: Before making any offer in St. Louis, run your numbers through our free Wholesale Deal Calculator. Plug in your purchase price, estimated rehab, and ARV to instantly see your potential profit margin and maximum allowable offer (MAO). Deals that look attractive on the surface often fall apart when you account for holding costs, closing fees, and agent commissions.
St. Louis Real Estate Market Trends for 2024

Despite national market turbulence driven by rising interest rates, St. Louis has remained relatively stable. Days on market have increased slightly — from an average of 18 days in 2022 to closer to 28 to 35 days in 2024 — which is actually good news for investors. More time on market means more motivated sellers and less competition from retail buyers. Inventory has also ticked up in the county, creating better opportunities for buyers who were priced out during the 2021-2022 frenzy.

One of the biggest trends shaping the St. Louis market right now is the growing demand for off-market deals. As MLS competition heats up even in affordable markets, investors who can find properties before they hit the open market are winning consistently. Understanding how to build a direct-to-seller pipeline is essential — read our full breakdown on How to Find Off-Market Real Estate Deals for proven strategies that work specifically well in second-tier Midwest markets like St. Louis.

"The best real estate deals aren't found on the MLS — they're found in relationships with motivated sellers before anyone else knows the property is available." — Common wisdom among top St. Louis wholesalers and investors
Tips for Out-of-State Investors Targeting St. Louis

St. Louis is one of the most popular markets for remote investors, and for good reason. Low price points mean less capital at risk while you learn the market, and strong property management infrastructure makes it viable to operate from anywhere in the country. That said, remote investing here does come with a learning curve. You need to understand hyper-local neighborhood dynamics — a few blocks can mean the difference between a solid rental and a vacant headache.

items: Hire a local property manager before you buy: Management fees of 8% to 10% are standard in St. Louis and are absolutely worth it if you're not local. Interview at least three before committing.

Visit at least once before scaling: A single market visit will teach you more about St. Louis neighborhoods than hours of Zillow browsing. Drive the streets, talk to local investors, and attend a local REIA meetup.
Build a reliable contractor network: Rehab quality varies wildly in St. Louis. Get at least three bids on any project and ask for references from local investors — not just homeowners.

Understand the tax delinquency system: St. Louis has a robust tax sale process that can yield incredible acquisition opportunities. Research the annual Land Tax Sale and Collector's Auction for deeply discounted properties.
Analyze every deal like a pro: Remote investors can't afford sloppy underwriting. Learn how to analyze real estate deals like a pro before you wire any earnest money.

Join local Facebook groups and BiggerPockets forums: The St. Louis investing community is surprisingly active and collaborative. Many deals are shared informally among investors before ever hitting any formal marketplace.

sections.content: Pro Tip: When evaluating St. Louis rentals remotely, always request a full interior walkthrough video from your agent or property manager — not just photos. St. Louis has a significant number of properties with deferred maintenance that photographs well but has hidden structural or mechanical issues that will destroy your cash flow.
Why St. Louis Remains One of the Best Markets for Value Investors

At its core, St. Louis is a value investor's market. You won't see the explosive appreciation of Austin or Miami here, but you will find consistent cash flow, deep discount opportunities, and a real estate ecosystem that rewards patient, disciplined investors who do their homework. With a major medical corridor, several large universities, a growing tech scene anchored by companies like Centene and Square, and a historically stable employment base, the city's fundamentals are sound. For investors who know how to find deals and analyze them accurately, St. Louis continues to deliver strong returns year after year.
